resources.string: Before starting work,\nit is necessary to connect the model.

Here, you specify the exact AI model you want to call. For cloud services, you must enter the precise model name used in the API; this is always listed in the provider's documentation. For local models, enter the name of the model you downloaded and are running in your program.\nExample:

If you are using a cloud service, enter the provider's official address here. You can find the exact address in the service's documentation. If you are running the model locally on your computer, the address always starts with `http://localhost` and includes the port number displayed by the program itself. You can see this address in the running program's interface.\nExample:

This is a secret key that verifies your right to use the model. For cloud services, the key is issued when you register on the provider's website. It appears as a long string of letters, numbers, and symbols. You need to copy it from your account dashboard and paste it into this field. Keep this key confidential and do not share it with anyone. No key is required for local models running on your computer.\nExample:

Enter a number here representing the time (in seconds) the program will wait for a response from the model before terminating the connection and reporting a connection failure.\nIf the model is fast or you are sending short requests, you can set this to 30 or 60 seconds. If the model is computationally intensive, slow, or generates large amounts of text, it is better to increase the value to 120 or even 180 seconds.\nExample:
